messages.subject: Laplace approx. by hand
parts:
Hi guys,

Using the https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/laplace_8cpp-example.html as example I'm trying to build the Laplace approx. in a multinomial GLMM with a non-standard link function in the context of repeated measures.

The laplace Functor is the same, I changed the joint and the marginal (objective function) for my specific case. However, I'm not being able to successfully compile the cpp.

The main difference from the spatial example is that since I have several subjects, I need to compute the Laplace approx. for each one of them. So I thought to do that in a loop

  // random/latent effect initial guess
  // each row of U is for one subject
  // nc is the number of subjects
  matrix<Type> U(nc, 4);
  U.setZero();
  Type res = 0;
  int niter = 10;
  // each subject has two measurements and my multinomial has three classes 
  matrix<Type> y(2, 3);
  int j = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < nc; i++) {
      y.row(0) = Y.row(j);
      y.row(1) = Y.row(j + 1);
      // construct joint negative log-likelihood
      joint_nll<Type> jnll(y, time.segment(j, 2), delta,
                                         beta1, beta2, gama1, gama2, w1, w2,
                                         sigma, theta);
      j += 2;
      // calculate Laplace approx. (updates u)
      vector<Type> u = U.row(i);
       res += laplace(jnll, u, niter);
  }
  return res;

Looking to this piece of code something appears to be wrong?
My laplace is the same from the example, and besides that piece, the rest of the marginal is just definition of variables.

I don't know if my problem is in the joint, or if something is missing in the laplace, or I shouldn't do the integration in a loop... I don't know.

The whole file follow attached.

Tks!!
H

messages.author: 2ef9a687f7364fdc
messages.subject: Re: Laplace approx. by hand
parts:
Eigen objects (e.g., vector matrix, array) should be casted using 'template cast'.

For example:

// vector<Type> time;
// Type delta;
vector<T> ddle = delta/(2 * time * (delta - time));


should be:

vector<T> time_T = time.template cast<T>();
vector<T> ddle = (T)delta/((T)2 * time_T * ((T)delta - time_T));

- Christoffer
